findings.summary: No test covers the one line that makes #878 work: if `results = await _cooldowns.AfterRoundAsync(...)` is deleted, every test stays green. S22–S25 call AfterRoundAsync directly, S26–S29 hand-write quota-cooldowns.json, and no test under src_mcp/tests names QuotaCooldowns on the RoundEngine path. The same gap covers PanelService passing its launcher and `noticing.Offer` into the store.
findings.fix: Add a round-level test using the RoundNamesTheExcludedTests / PanelService harness with a scripted launcher. Round 1: an agy row refuses with AGY_1_3_3 (exit 3) and the /quota probe answers with QUOTA_SAMPLE. Then assert that quota-cooldowns.json parks antigravity/gemini and that ExcludedFrom for the next round names the row. Delete the AfterRoundAsync line once and watch the test go red.

findings.summary: Commit aa74be74 removed the `.badge.verdict.cooling` rule but dropped a line break with it, so CATALOG_BADGES (the badge sheet the Team tab shares) now has two rules on one line. That is out of scope. It also makes the re-pin comment in teamServerTab.test.ts:211-214 false. Checked: removing `, .catalog .cooldown-line` from the current sheet hashes to 032a34ef…, not the claimed previous pin 862e9808…. The old pin only comes back when the line break is restored too.
findings.fix: Put the line break back between the `.badge.verdict.ok` rule and the `.badge.health.ok::before` rule, then re-pin CATALOG_CSS so the hash differs from 862e9808… only by the added `.cooldown-line` selector.

findings.summary: Apply calls HeldFile.TakeWithin synchronously. TakeWithin waits in a Thread.Sleep loop for up to the 30 s default, and here it runs inside the async AfterRoundAsync on the round path. While the lock is contended this blocks a thread-pool thread, which common.reliability forbids ('a blocking lock is never taken directly on an async worker thread'). ConsultantPlaces.cs:125 moves the same call off the calling thread with Task.Run.
findings.fix: Take the lock off the calling thread as ConsultantPlaces does: `await Task.Run(() => HeldFile.TakeWithin(...), ct)`, or make Apply async. Keep Busy and Unusable as refusals.

findings.summary: Every keyed row that answers Ok gets a Lift, even when nothing is parked. So almost every round creates the lock file, takes the lock and re-reads the JSON. When the lock is busy, that no-op lift is refused, logs a warning and posts a 'a spent quota could not be remembered' server notice although nothing was lost.
findings.fix: Only queue Change.Lift for a key that has an entry in the file (check with an unlocked Read or Standing first), so a round with nothing to change takes no lock and posts no notice.

findings.summary: ResetOf parses reset_time with DateTimeStyles.None, so a timestamp with no offset is read in the server's local zone and can park hours off. Separately, Parse/Documents (line 133) creates JsonDocument instances and never disposes them.
findings.fix: Use DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal (as QuotaCooldowns.Instant does) or refuse a reset_time that has no offset. Dispose each JsonDocument after the report is copied out of it, for example by materialising inside a `using`.

findings.summary: S34's round half does not match the plan, and §12 does not record it. The plan says both agy rows ended spent; the test makes the Gemini row undecided (`Spent(Transient, null)`). The coder had to change it: under D5/S41 an explicitly spent Gemini refusal with an Available gauge is parked on `stated`, so the plan's literal S34 contradicts its own S41. Also, S14 is named `AnUnknownModel_HasNoGroup_AndEveryKnownOneHasItsKey`, not the plan's exact `AnUnknownModel_HasNoGroup` (TheAgyQuotaReportPicksTheResetTests.cs:79).
findings.fix: Record both as deviations in §12 of the plan: S34's Gemini row is undecided because D5/S41 would park an explicitly spent one, and S14's test name was changed. Or rename the S14 test to the plan's name.
